source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Internal Organisation of Plants
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Intercalary meristems that restore growth after grazing are typical of
questions.explanation: Grasses keep intercalary meristems at internodes/nodes, so shoots elongate after the tip is removed.

questions.stem: Living mechanical tissue with irregularly thickened cellulose walls at the corners is
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living and provide flexible support; sclerenchyma fibres are typically dead and lignified.

questions.stem: In a typical dicot root, protoxylem lies toward the periphery. This xylem is
questions.explanation: Roots have exarch xylem (protoxylem outside, metaxylem inside); stems are usually endarch.

questions.stem: Sieve-tube members of angiosperm phloem are metabolically supported by
questions.explanation: Companion cells are sister cells of sieve-tube elements and keep them alive through plasmodesmata.

questions.stem: Stomatal pores are bounded by specialised epidermal cells called
questions.explanation: A stoma is a pore between two guard cells that regulate gas exchange and transpiration.

questions.stem: Casparian strips of suberin occur in the
questions.explanation: Endodermal radial and transverse walls bear Casparian strips that force water into the symplast.

questions.stem: Scattered closed vascular bundles with a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath are typical of
questions.explanation: Monocot stems have many scattered, usually closed (no cambium) vascular bundles.

questions.stem: Palisade parenchyma is usually well developed on the adaxial side of a
questions.explanation: Dorsiventral (dicot) leaves have palisade toward the upper surface and spongy tissue below.

questions.stem: The lateral meristem that produces secondary xylem and secondary phloem is the
questions.explanation: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem: inner derivatives become wood, outer derivatives become bast.

questions.stem: A siphonostele differs from a protostele because the vascular cylinder
options: is confined to the leaf only
questions.explanation: Protosteles have a solid xylem core; siphonosteles are tubular with a pith in the centre.

questions.stem: Which simple tissue is typically dead at maturity and has uniformly lignified thick walls?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma (fibres and sclereids) is usually dead and lignified; collenchyma remains living.

questions.stem: Bicollateral open vascular bundles, with phloem on both sides of xylem, are a textbook feature of
questions.explanation: Cucurbit stems have bicollateral bundles (outer phloem–xylem–inner phloem) with cambium.

questions.stem: Choose the correct pair about secondary growth. I. Phellogen produces phellem toward the outside. II. Heartwood is the outer living xylem that conducts sap. III. Annual rings reflect seasonal activity of vascular cambium.
questions.explanation: Phellogen cuts off cork outward; heartwood is the inner non-conducting wood, not the living sapwood.

questions.stem: Apical meristems responsible for primary growth are located at the
questions.explanation: Shoot and root apices bear apical meristems that add primary tissues and length.

questions.stem: Chlorenchyma is a photosynthetic form of
questions.explanation: Parenchyma with chloroplasts is called chlorenchyma and is common in leaf mesophyll.

questions.stem: The only living component among typical xylem elements is
questions.explanation: Tracheary elements and most xylem fibres die at maturity; xylem parenchyma remains living.

questions.stem: Which phloem cell is absent in most gymnosperms but present in angiosperms?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms have sieve tubes plus companion cells; gymnosperms have sieve cells and albuminous cells.

questions.stem: Unicellular or multicellular outgrowths of the epidermis such as hairs are collectively called
questions.explanation: Trichomes are epidermal appendages; they may reduce transpiration or secrete substances.

questions.stem: A polyarch, usually more than six, xylem-phloem arrangement with a large pith is typical of
questions.explanation: Monocot roots are polyarch with a well-developed pith; dicot roots are usually tetrarch or pentarch with little pith.

questions.stem: Open vascular bundles arranged in a ring around a pith characterise a typical
questions.explanation: Dicot stems have a eustele: bundles in a ring, usually open (cambium present).

questions.stem: An isobilateral leaf, as in many grasses, typically has stomata
options: on both surfaces in similar numbers
questions.explanation: Isobilateral leaves are amphistomatic; dorsiventral dicot leaves are often hypostomatic.

questions.stem: Cork cambium (phellogen) and its products phellem and phelloderm together form the
questions.explanation: Periderm = phellem + phellogen + phelloderm, the protective secondary covering after epidermis is lost.

questions.stem: Conjoint, collateral and closed vascular bundles means
options: xylem and phloem on the same radius, cambium absent
xylem and phloem on opposite radii, cambium present
phloem surrounding xylem on all sides
only phloem present in the bundle
questions.explanation: Collateral: phloem outside xylem on one radius; closed: no intrafascicular cambium (typical monocot stem).

questions.stem: Which statement about meristems is incorrect?
options: Intercalary meristems occur at grass nodes.
The root cap itself is a permanent lateral meristem.
questions.explanation: The root cap is a protective tissue produced by the root apical meristem, not a lateral meristem.

questions.stem: Passage cells in the root endodermis are
options: dead cork cells of the periderm
companion cells of the leaf phloem
questions.explanation: Opposite protoxylem, some endodermal cells stay thin-walled and permit radial transport.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match of organ and anatomical feature.
options: Dicot root — exarch xylem, usually tetrarch
Dicot stem — open bundles in a ring
Monocot root — typically diarch xylem and no pith
questions.explanation: Monocot roots are polyarch with a large pith; a diarch pattern with little pith is a dicot-root type.
